  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

验证者与边缘节点机群管理平台：长期产品目标

## 产品定位

建设一个验证者与边缘节点机群管理平台。产品应以清晰的领域模型和稳定接口承载真实业务增长，在正确性、可审计性、可观测性与运维可控性之间取得平衡，并能在本机离线、可复现地运行。

## 产品范围

- 节点注册与身份：验证者与边缘设备的注册、身份绑定与生命周期。
- 心跳与遥测：在线状态、高度、版本、资源与网络指标采集。
- 离线同步：断连期间的本地缓冲、恢复后的补传与一致性。
- 配置分发与升级：灰度分组、滚动升级、失败回滚与版本冻结。
- 健康与罚没规则：漏签、停机与版本偏移的规则判断与告警。
- 运维记录：远程操作的完整留痕与审计。

## 核心质量目标

- 状态判断必须基于真实遥测，不能用缺省值当作健康。
- 升级与回滚幂等，部分成功不得报告为全部成功。
- 离线节点恢复后不产生重复或丢失的职责记录。

## 技术方向

主要技术方向：validator, node-monitoring, device-fleet, p2p-network, telemetry, devnet。实现以 Go 标准库为主，全部行为可在单机离线环境复现。

## 演进规则

每一轮工作都必须依据当前冻结源码提出真实产品演进，覆盖 feature 迭代、Bug 修复、代码重构、工程化、代码测试、代码理解以及必要的 0-1 子系统建设。
优先选择困难或地狱级任务，强调并发安全、时间语义、幂等性、数据一致性、故障恢复、查询性能、规则冲突、可审计性、兼容迁移与确定性测试等需要系统推理的边界。
不得为凑数重复已有能力、只改文案，或引入与产品价值无关的复杂度；也不得依赖不可用的外部服务或真实链上网络。

## 验收取向

每题都必须具有可独立验收的用户价值：行为可由命令行或测试确定性复现，失败与成功都能被真实观察。
真实产品测试失败须保留原样并给出归因，不要求全部断言通过；环境缺失、未执行与超时不得算作产品缺陷。

1	package edgefleet

15	
16	// AggregateResult is one closed window output line.
17	type AggregateResult struct {
18		Key   string `json:"key"`
19		Start int64  `json:"start"`
20		End   int64  `json:"end"`
21		Count int64  `json:"count"`
22		Sum   int64  `json:"sum"`
23	}
24	
25	// InputError reports a fatal problem with one physical input line.
26	type InputError struct {
27		Line   int
28		Reason string
29	}
30	
31	func (e *InputError) Error() string {
32		return fmt.Sprintf("line %d: %s", e.Line, e.Reason)
33	}
34	
35	// OutputError reports that output triggered by one physical input line could
36	// not be written in full. Line is that input line (blank lines count), and
37	// Kind is either "window result" or "late-event notice". Detail identifies
38	// the record: a window's key and [start,end), or the skipped event time and
39	// the watermark used to judge it. Err is the writer's own error, including
40	// when only a prefix was accepted before it failed; when the writer reported
41	// no error but accepted too few bytes, Err is io.ErrShortWrite. Use
42	// errors.Is to inspect it. Content the writer already accepted stays in
43	// place and fully written earlier results stay valid.
44	type OutputError struct {
45		Line   int
46		Kind   string
47		Detail string
48		Err    error
49	}
50	
51	func (e *OutputError) Error() string {
52		return fmt.Sprintf("line %d: %s not fully written (%s): %v", e.Line, e.Kind, e.Detail, e.Err)
53	}
54	
55	func (e *OutputError) Unwrap() error {
56		return e.Err
57	}
58	
59	// writeFull writes all of p to w in one call. Any writer error is returned
60	// unchanged, even when the writer accepted a prefix first, so callers keep
61	// errors.Is access to the original error. A nil error with fewer than
62	// len(p) accepted bytes is reported as io.ErrShortWrite; writeFull never
63	// retries or resends the missing tail.
64	func writeFull(w io.Writer, p []byte) error {
65		n, err := w.Write(p)
66		if err != nil {
67			return err
68		}
69		if n < len(p) {
70			return io.ErrShortWrite
71		}
72		return nil
73	}
74	
75	// AggregateParamName identifies which aggregate start parameter a
76	// *AggregateParamError reports.
77	type AggregateParamName string
78	
79	const (
80		// AggregateParamWindow is the window length (--window-ms).
81		AggregateParamWindow AggregateParamName = "window"
82		// AggregateParamSlide is the slide interval (--slide-ms).
83		AggregateParamSlide AggregateParamName = "slide"
84		// AggregateParamPartitions is the partition count (--partitions).
85		AggregateParamPartitions AggregateParamName = "partitions"
86	)

89	// one parameter.
90	type AggregateParamKind string
91	
92	const (
93		// AggregateParamNotPositive means the value was zero or negative where a
94		// positive signed 64-bit integer is required.
95		AggregateParamNotPositive AggregateParamKind = "not_positive"
96		// AggregateParamTooLarge means the slide interval exceeds the window
97		// length. It is reported for AggregateParamSlide and carries the window
98		// length in Limit.
99		AggregateParamTooLarge AggregateParamKind = "too_large"
100	)
101	
102	// AggregateParamError reports one invalid aggregate start parameter. It is the
103	// single source of the shared startup parameter limits: every aggregate entry
104	// point (the library runners and the command line) funnels its numeric
105	// parameter checks through ValidateAggregateParams, so the same restriction is
106	// stated in one place. Which parameter may be omitted, and what an omitted or
107	// zero value means, is entry-specific and decided by the caller; this reports
108	// only the limits common to every entry. Field identifies the parameter, Kind
109	// the violated limit, Value the rejected value and Limit the window length for
110	// AggregateParamTooLarge (zero otherwise). Error renders the library entry
111	// point's existing wording, which callers may rephrase for their own surface
112	// while keeping the field-driven decision identical.
113	type AggregateParamError struct {
114		Field AggregateParamName
115		Kind  AggregateParamKind
116		Value int64
117		Limit int64
118	}
119	
120	func (e *AggregateParamError) Error() string {
121		switch e.Kind {
122		case AggregateParamTooLarge:
123			return fmt.Sprintf("slide interval %d must not exceed window length %d", e.Value, e.Limit)
124		case AggregateParamNotPositive:
125			switch e.Field {
126			case AggregateParamWindow:
127				return fmt.Sprintf("window length must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d", e.Value)
128			case AggregateParamSlide:
129				return fmt.Sprintf("slide interval must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d", e.Value)
130			case AggregateParamPartitions:
131				return fmt.Sprintf("partition count must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d", e.Value)
132			}
133		}
134		return fmt.Sprintf("invalid aggregate parameter %s: %d", e.Field, e.Value)
135	}

137	// ValidateAggregateParams enforces the aggregate startup limits shared by every
138	// entry point, in the order they have always been reported: window length,
139	// then slide interval, then the slide-vs-window comparison, then the partition
140	// count. windowMillis must be a positive signed 64-bit integer. slideMillis
141	// must be a positive signed 64-bit integer no greater than windowMillis; it
142	// does not have to divide windowMillis, and equality is the fixed-window case.
143	// partitions must not be negative; zero itself is accepted here because the
144	// library entry points use it to select legacy single-watermark mode -- an
145	// entry that rejects an explicitly supplied zero (the command line) keeps that
146	// policy of its own before or around this call. The first violated limit is
147	// returned as *AggregateParamError; nil means the parameters are sound and the
148	// caller may start reading input, so no invalid configuration ever reaches the
149	// input reader.
150	func ValidateAggregateParams(windowMillis, slideMillis, partitions int64) error {
151		if windowMillis <= 0 {
152			return &AggregateParamError{Field: AggregateParamWindow, Kind: AggregateParamNotPositive, Value: windowMillis}
153		}
154		if slideMillis <= 0 {
155			return &AggregateParamError{Field: AggregateParamSlide, Kind: AggregateParamNotPositive, Value: slideMillis}
156		}
157		if slideMillis > windowMillis {
158			return &AggregateParamError{Field: AggregateParamSlide, Kind: AggregateParamTooLarge, Value: slideMillis, Limit: windowMillis}
159		}
160		if partitions < 0 {
161			return &AggregateParamError{Field: AggregateParamPartitions, Kind: AggregateParamNotPositive, Value: partitions}
162		}
163		return nil
164	}

166	type windowID struct {
167		start int64 // inclusive window start in milliseconds since time zero
168		key   string
169	}

171	type windowState struct {
172		end   int64 // exclusive window end in milliseconds
173		count int64
174		sum   int64
175	}

177	// RunAggregate reads line-delimited JSON records from r and writes closed
178	// fixed window results, one JSON object per line, to out. windowMillis must
179	// be a positive signed 64-bit integer. Windows are fixed-length, start at
180	// time zero and use a left-closed right-open interval. Closure is driven
181	// solely by input watermarks: a window whose end is less than or equal to the
182	// current watermark is emitted once, ordered by end ascending and then by key
183	// in UTF-8 byte order. Late events (event time below the current watermark)
184	// are reported on lateLog with their physical line number and skipped. Every
185	// output must land in full: a window result is its complete JSON object plus
186	// trailing newline and a late-event notice is its complete single line. If
187	// the corresponding writer returns an error after accepting zero bytes or
188	// only a prefix, or accepts too few bytes with no error, the run fails at
189	// once with *OutputError naming the triggering physical input line:
190	// window-result failures identify the key and window [start,end), and
191	// late-notice failures identify the skipped event time and the watermark
192	// used; a nil-error short write is io.ErrShortWrite and errors.Is exposes
193	// the writer's original error. After such a failure no further records are
194	// processed, the failed content is neither rewritten nor resent, and
195	// still-open windows produce no further results; content already accepted
196	// by the writers stays in place, including fully written earlier results.
197	// Fatal record problems return *InputError; results already written to out
198	// stay written, and open windows are not flushed at end of input. An event
199	// key that would lose characters when decoded -- invalid UTF-8 bytes, or a
200	// \u escape whose surrogate half is unpaired or mispaired -- is such a fatal
201	// problem: it is never repaired to U+FFFD and counted, so distinct damaged
202	// keys can never merge or collide with a key that is genuinely U+FFFD. The
203	// check runs before the late-event check, so a damaged key is fatal even
204	// below the current watermark.
205	//
206	// A read failure is distinct from reaching the end of input. Only a reader
207	// returning the bare io.EOF sentinel is a clean end, where a final record that
208	// arrived without a trailing newline is still processed (and a damaged one is
209	// an *InputError carrying its physical line number). A wrapped io.EOF or a
210	// combined error whose chain merely contains io.EOF is still a read failure.
211	// When r returns any error other than the bare io.EOF after delivering bytes,
212	// only records whose newline was already received are processed, in order,
213	// including records returned by the same Read that carried the error; the
214	// remaining unterminated bytes never become an event, watermark or idle
215	// declaration and can produce no late notice or window result, and the
216	// reader's own error is then returned unchanged so errors.Is exposes it. A
217	// record or output failure on one of those complete lines is reported
218	// instead of the read error discovered afterwards.
219	//
220	// This is the legacy single-watermark mode: records carry no partition field
221	// and any extra fields are ignored. Use RunAggregatePartitioned to merge
222	// several independent input sources of the same stream, or
223	// RunAggregateSliding to emit overlapping windows at a shorter interval.
224	func RunAggregate(r io.Reader, windowMillis int64, out io.Writer, lateLog io.Writer) error {
225		return RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(r, windowMillis, windowMillis, 0, out, lateLog)
226	}
227	
228	// RunAggregateSliding is RunAggregate with overlapping sliding windows. The
229	// window length is windowMillis and consecutive window starts are slideMillis
230	// apart, beginning at time zero: 0, slideMillis, 2*slideMillis, ... Each
231	// window is left-closed right-open and no window with a negative start is
232	// created. slideMillis must be a positive signed 64-bit integer no greater
233	// than windowMillis and does not have to divide it; slideMillis equal to
234	// windowMillis is exactly RunAggregate's fixed-window behavior. A valid event
235	// is counted once in every window that contains its event time, adding to
236	// that window's per-key count and the full value to its sum. Everything else
237	// (watermark-only closure, ordering, late reporting, overflow handling and
238	// end-of-input behavior) is identical to RunAggregate.
239	func RunAggregateSliding(r io.Reader, windowMillis, slideMillis int64, out io.Writer, lateLog io.Writer) error {
240		return RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(r, windowMillis, slideMillis, 0, out, lateLog)
241	}
242	
243	// RunAggregatePartitioned is RunAggregatePartitionedSliding with slideMillis
244	// equal to windowMillis (non-overlapping fixed windows).
245	func RunAggregatePartitioned(r io.Reader, windowMillis, partitions int64, out io.Writer, lateLog io.Writer) error {
246		return RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(r, windowMillis, windowMillis, partitions, out, lateLog)
247	}
248	
249	// RunAggregatePartitionedSliding combines sliding windows (see
250	// RunAggregateSliding) with partitioned inputs: events from different
251	// partitions merge into one count and sum per key and window, and both the
252	// late-event check and window closure use the effective (minimum) watermark.
253	// windowMillis and slideMillis are validated exactly as in
254	// RunAggregateSliding. partitions selects the input mode:
255	//
256	//   - partitions == 0: legacy single-watermark mode. Records do not carry a
257	//     partition field; any extra fields are ignored.
258	//
259	//   - partitions > 0: partitioned mode, merging partitions independent input
260	//     sources of the same stream. Every event and watermark record must carry
261	//     an integer "partition" in [0,partitions). Each partition advances its
262	//     own watermark; no effective watermark exists until every partition has
263	//     reported at least once, afterwards the effective watermark is the
264	//     minimum of the per-partition values. Window closure and late-event
265	//     checks use this minimum, so one partition's larger watermark can never
266	//     close a window or drop an event ahead of the others. A partition
267	//     watermark may repeat or jump forward but never move backwards.
268	//
269	//     A partition may be declared idle with
270	//     {"type":"idle","partition":p}. An idle partition stops contributing to
271	//     the effective watermark: non-idle partitions that have not reported a
272	//     watermark yet still keep the effective watermark unknown, while a
273	//     partition that never reported may itself be declared idle. When every
274	//     remaining (non-idle) partition has reported, the effective watermark is
275	//     their minimum and the idle record itself can close windows. If all
276	//     partitions are idle, the last produced effective watermark is retained;
277	//     when none was ever produced it stays unknown. Idleness is declared by
278	//     the input only, never inferred from time; a repeated idle declaration
279	//     is a no-op. The next watermark record for that partition resumes it:
280	//     its time must be at least both the partition's previous watermark and
281	//     the current effective watermark. An event for an idle partition is
282	//     fatal; it never resumes implicitly.
283	//
284	// partitions < 0 is an error. Windows, ordering, late-event reporting,
285	// overflow checks and end-of-input behavior are otherwise identical to
286	// RunAggregateSliding.
287	func RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(r io.Reader, windowMillis, slideMillis, partitions int64, out io.Writer, lateLog io.Writer) error {
288		if err := ValidateAggregateParams(windowMillis, slideMillis, partitions); err != nil {
289			return err
290		}
291		s := &aggregateState{
292			windowMillis:  windowMillis,
293			slideMillis:   slideMillis,
294			windows:       make(map[windowID]*windowState),
295			out:           out,
296			lateLog:       lateLog,
297			partitions:    partitions,
298			partWatermark: make(map[int64]*int64),
299			idle:          make(map[int64]bool),
300		}
301	
302		// Read records with a line collector that keeps a read failure distinct
303		// from end of input: only newline-terminated lines (plus, at a clean EOF,
304		// one unterminated final line) ever become records.
305		lineNo := 0
306		err := readAggregateLines(r, func(line string, no int) error {
307			lineNo = no
308			if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
309				return nil
310			}
311			return s.processLine(line, lineNo)
312		})
313		return err
314	}
315	
316	// maxAggregateLineBytes caps the size of a single physical input line, matching
317	// the scanner buffer limit this used to run with. A line this long is fatal
318	// before its record is parsed.
319	const maxAggregateLineBytes = 1024 * 1024 * 1024
320	
321	// errAggregateLineTooLong reports a physical input line that never ends within
322	// maxAggregateLineBytes.
323	var errAggregateLineTooLong = errors.New("aggregate input line longer than 1 GiB")
324	
325	// errAggregateBadReadCount reports an io.Reader that handed back a byte count
326	// outside the destination buffer, violating the io.Reader contract.
327	var errAggregateBadReadCount = errors.New("aggregate reader returned an impossible byte count")
328	
329	// readAggregateLines feeds newline-delimited physical lines from r to handle,
330	// counting every line (a bare "\n" is a blank line too) and stripping a single
331	// trailing '\r' so CRLF input works as before. Clean end of input and a
332	// non-EOF read failure are handled differently: only the bare io.EOF
333	// sentinel is a clean end, and then a final line missing its newline is still
334	// delivered, exactly like every other final record; a wrapped io.EOF or a
335	// combined error whose chain contains io.EOF is a failure, not an end. After
336	// any error other than the bare io.EOF only lines whose newline was already
337	// received (including those delivered by the same Read that carried the
338	// error) are handled, in order, and then the reader's original error is
339	// returned. The unterminated tail never reaches handle, so a read failure
340	// mid-record can neither be misreported as an input error nor produce
341	// events, watermarks, idle declarations, late notices or window results. A
342	// non-nil error from handle stops reading immediately and replaces the read
343	// error, so an earlier record or output failure is not overwritten by a
344	// failure the reader only reports later.
345	func readAggregateLines(r io.Reader, handle func(line string, lineNo int) error) error {
346		// buf[start:end] is the undelivered tail; buf[:start] is space freed by
347		// already delivered lines. The buffer is compacted and grown like
348		// bufio.Scanner's, so a long unterminated line is bounded by
349		// maxAggregateLineBytes instead of growing without limit.
350		//
351		// searchFrom is the earliest absolute index not yet inspected for a '\n':
352		// every byte before it has either been delivered or searched already. A
353		// Read can only introduce a newline in the bytes it just appended, so the
354		// pending tail of a long line is never rescanned; scanning, compaction and
355		// growth together stay linear in the cumulative byte count even when each
356		// Read brings a single byte. searchFrom >= start always holds, and
357		// compaction/growth shift every absolute index by the same start they do.
358		buf := make([]byte, 64*1024)
359		start, end := 0, 0
360		searchFrom := 0
361		lineNo := 0
362		emptyReads := 0
363		deliver := func(b []byte) error {
364			lineNo++
365			line := strings.TrimSuffix(string(b), "\r")
366			return handle(line, lineNo)
367		}
368		for {
369			// Move the pending tail to the front when its freed prefix is large
370			// enough or when the whole buffer is pending.
371			if start > 0 && (end == len(buf) || start > len(buf)/2) {
372				copy(buf, buf[start:end])
373				end -= start
374				searchFrom -= start
375				if searchFrom < 0 {
376					searchFrom = 0
377				}
378				start = 0
379			}
380			if end == len(buf) {
381				// No newline fit before the end: the physical line is too long.
382				if len(buf) >= maxAggregateLineBytes {
383					return errAggregateLineTooLong
384				}
385				newLen := len(buf) * 2
386				if newLen > maxAggregateLineBytes || newLen < len(buf) {
387					newLen = maxAggregateLineBytes
388				}
389				grown := make([]byte, newLen)
390				copy(grown, buf[start:end])
391				buf = grown
392				end -= start
393				searchFrom -= start
394				if searchFrom < 0 {
395					searchFrom = 0
396				}
397				start = 0
398			}
399			n, readErr := r.Read(buf[end:])
400			if n < 0 || n > len(buf)-end {
401				// A Reader must never report a byte count outside the buffer.
402				return errAggregateBadReadCount
403			}
404			end += n
405			// Only this Read's newly appended bytes can still hold an unseen
406			// newline; search from searchFrom rather than from start, so a long
407			// line delivered a few bytes at a time costs one scan of each byte
408			// instead of one scan per Read over the whole accumulated tail.
409			for searchFrom < end {
410				i := bytes.IndexByte(buf[searchFrom:end], '\n')
411				if i < 0 {
412					break
413				}
414				idx := searchFrom + i
415				if err := deliver(buf[start:idx]); err != nil {
416					return err
417				}
418				start = idx + 1
419				searchFrom = start
420			}
421			searchFrom = end
422			if readErr != nil {
423				if readErr == io.EOF {
424					// Clean end of input: a trailing line without a newline is a
425					// complete final record; an empty tail (input ending exactly
426					// on '\n') is nothing, not an extra blank line. Only the
427					// bare io.EOF sentinel counts -- a wrapped EOF or a combined
428					// error whose chain contains io.EOF is a read failure, never
429					// a clean end.
430					if end > start {
431						if err := deliver(buf[start:end]); err != nil {
432							return err
433						}
434					}
435					return nil
436				}
437				// Any other failure means the stream stopped mid-record: the
438				// still-unterminated bytes are not a record. Surface the original
439				// error unchanged so errors.Is keeps working for callers.
440				return readErr
441			}
442			if n == 0 {
443				// No data and no error: refuse to spin forever on a broken Reader.
444				emptyReads++
445				if emptyReads > 100 {
446					return io.ErrNoProgress
447				}
448			} else {
449				emptyReads = 0
450			}
451		}
452	}

454	type aggregateState struct {
455		windowMillis int64
456		slideMillis  int64 // distance between consecutive window starts; equals windowMillis for fixed windows
457		windows      map[windowID]*windowState
458		out          io.Writer
459		lateLog      io.Writer
460	
461		partitions    int64 // 0 = legacy single-watermark mode
462		watermark     *int64
463		partWatermark map[int64]*int64 // partition -> last watermark; partitioned mode only
464		idle          map[int64]bool   // partitions declared idle in the input; partitioned mode only
465	}
466	
467	func (s *aggregateState) processLine(line string, lineNo int) error {
468		var obj map[string]json.RawMessage
469		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
470			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: "invalid JSON record: " + err.Error()}
471		}
472	
473		typeRaw, ok := obj["type"]
474		if !ok {
475			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: `missing required string field "type"`}
476		}
477		recordType, err := decodeString(typeRaw, "type")
478		if err != nil {
479			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: err.Error()}
480		}
481	
482		switch recordType {
483		case "event":
484			return s.processEvent(obj, lineNo)
485		case "watermark":
486			return s.processWatermark(obj, lineNo)
487		case "idle":
488			// Only partitioned mode knows idle declarations; legacy
489			// single-watermark mode treats it as any unknown record type.
490			if s.partitions == 0 {
491				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("unknown record type %q", recordType)}
492			}
493			return s.processIdle(obj, lineNo)
494		default:
495			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("unknown record type %q", recordType)}
496		}
497	}
498	
499	// floorDiv returns math.Floor(a/b) for b > 0; Go's / truncates toward zero,
500	// so negative numerators need explicit adjustment.
501	func floorDiv(a, b int64) int64 {
502		q := a / b
503		if a%b != 0 && a < 0 {
504			q--
505		}
506		return q
507	}
508	
509	// containingWindows describes every window that contains one event time, in
510	// one derivation shared by the normal counting path and the window-end
511	// overflow precheck: how many windows there are, where each starts, and which
512	// (if any) is the earliest whose end leaves the signed 64-bit range. Windows
513	// start at 0, slide, 2*slide, ... and none with a negative start is created,
514	// so the first index is clamped to zero. The last index is
515	// eventTime/slide, so an event at a window end is outside that window.
516	type containingWindows struct {
517		count     int64 // how many windows contain the event time
518		lastStart int64 // start of the last (highest) containing window
519		slide     int64 // distance between consecutive window starts
520		// firstOverflow is the start of the earliest containing window whose end
521		// (start + windowMillis) leaves the signed 64-bit range, or -1 when every
522		// containing window fits. Containing starts are an ascending arithmetic
523		// sequence with step slide, so overflow (if any) is a suffix and this is
524		// its first member.
525		firstOverflow int64
526	}
527	
528	// containingWindows derives the containing-window range for eventTime.
529	func (s *aggregateState) containingWindows(eventTime int64) containingWindows {
530		last := eventTime / s.slideMillis
531		first := floorDiv(eventTime-s.windowMillis, s.slideMillis) + 1
532		if first < 0 {
533			first = 0
534		}
535		w := containingWindows{
536			count:         last - first + 1,
537			lastStart:     eventTime - eventTime%s.slideMillis,
538			slide:         s.slideMillis,
539			firstOverflow: -1,
540		}
541		lowest := w.start(w.count - 1) // earliest containing start; never negative
542		maxSafeStart := int64(math.MaxInt64 - s.windowMillis)
543		switch {
544		case lowest > maxSafeStart:
545			w.firstOverflow = lowest
546		default:
547			safe := (maxSafeStart-lowest)/s.slideMillis + 1 // containing starts that fit
548			if safe < w.count {
549				// Reach back from lastStart, which is at most eventTime, so the
550				// subtraction cannot leave the signed 64-bit range.
551				w.firstOverflow = w.start(w.count - 1 - safe)
552			}
553		}
554		return w
555	}
556	
557	// start returns the start of the containing window reached back by offset
558	// indices from the last one (offset 0 = last window).
559	func (w containingWindows) start(offset int64) int64 {
560		return w.lastStart - offset*w.slide
561	}
562	
563	// eventRecord is one input event whose record content has already been
564	// interpreted and validated independently of aggregate state: key, time,
565	// value and (in partitioned mode) partition are final. Nothing about idle
566	// partitions, watermarks or windows has been inspected yet, so producing one
567	// never mutates -- or even reads -- window state.
568	type eventRecord struct {
569		key       string
570		time      int64
571		value     int64
572		partition int64 // partitioned mode only; always 0 in legacy mode
573	}
574	
575	// parseEventRecord is the interpretation half of event intake. It reads and
576	// checks the record's own fields and never consults aggregate state, so field
577	// legality is fully decided before any idle, late or window rule runs. Fields
578	// are validated in the order they have always been rejected: key, then time,
579	// then value, then partition. The key is decoded strictly: an empty key,
580	// invalid UTF-8 bytes and an unpaired or mispaired surrogate half are record
581	// errors, never content repaired to U+FFFD that could merge keys. In legacy
582	// mode (partitioned == false) extra fields -- including any stray partition
583	// field -- stay ignored and partition is reported as zero.
584	func parseEventRecord(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, partitioned bool, partitionCount int64, lineNo int) (eventRecord, error) {
585		key, err := requiredKey(obj, lineNo)
586		if err != nil {
587			return eventRecord{}, err
588		}
589		if key == "" {
590			return eventRecord{}, &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: `field "key" must be a non-empty string`}
591		}
592		eventTime, err := requiredNonNegInt64(obj, "time", lineNo)
593		if err != nil {
594			return eventRecord{}, err
595		}
596		value, err := requiredInt64(obj, "value", lineNo)
597		if err != nil {
598			return eventRecord{}, err
599		}
600		var partition int64
601		if partitioned {
602			partition, err = requiredPartitionField(obj, partitionCount, lineNo)
603			if err != nil {
604				return eventRecord{}, err
605			}
606		}
607		return eventRecord{
608			key:       key,
609			time:      eventTime,
610			value:     value,
611			partition: partition,
612		}, nil
613	}
614	
615	func (s *aggregateState) processEvent(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, lineNo int) error {
616		// Stage 1: interpret and validate the record's own content without
617		// touching aggregate state.
618		ev, err := parseEventRecord(obj, s.partitions > 0, s.partitions, lineNo)
619		if err != nil {
620			return err
621		}
622		// Stage 2: apply the validated event to aggregate state.
623		return s.acceptEvent(ev, lineNo)
624	}
625	
626	// acceptEvent is the state half of event intake: it applies one record that
627	// parseEventRecord has already fully validated, in the same order as before
628	// the split -- idle partition first, then the global-watermark late rule, and
629	// only afterwards the window counts. It never re-reads or re-validates record
630	// fields, so a field problem can never be downgraded to an idle failure or a
631	// late notice here. Partitioned mode judges lateness against the overall
632	// effective watermark; an event on an idle partition stays fatal and never
633	// resumes the partition implicitly. A strictly late event is skipped with the
634	// existing notice; an event time equal to the watermark still enters its
635	// windows.
636	func (s *aggregateState) acceptEvent(ev eventRecord, lineNo int) error {
637		if s.partitions > 0 && s.idle[ev.partition] {
638			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("event for idle partition %d is not allowed; send a watermark to resume it first", ev.partition)}
639		}
640	
641		if s.watermark != nil && ev.time < *s.watermark {

12	// The result contract for long records split across arbitrary reads lives in
13	// aggregate_long_record_test.go and aggregate_chunked_input_test.go. What is

15	// arrives one or a few bytes per Read, line collection must cost about one
16	// newline scan per input byte -- linear in the cumulative input byte count
17	// and read count -- rather than one scan per Read over the whole accumulated
18	// tail, which is quadratic in the line length.
19	
20	// singleByteCuts lists a cut before every byte except the first, the schedule
21	// that made the old rescanner quadratic.
22	func singleByteCuts(n int) []int {
23		cuts := make([]int, 0, n-1)
24		for at := 1; at < n; at++ {
25			cuts = append(cuts, at)
26		}
27		return cuts
28	}
29	
30	// bestSingleByteTime measures repeated one-byte-per-Read passes in growing
31	// batches until a batch spans at least minBatch, returning the best
32	// (minimum-noise) average per pass. Comparing two streams of the same byte
33	// length under the same schedule makes the ratio independent of the
34	// machine's absolute speed.
35	func bestSingleByteTime(t *testing.T, input string, minBatch time.Duration) time.Duration {
36		t.Helper()
37		cuts := singleByteCuts(len(input))
38		iters := 1
39		best := time.Duration(1<<63 - 1)
40		for attempt := 0; attempt < 6; attempt++ {
41			begin := time.Now()
42			for i := 0; i < iters; i++ {
43				var out, late bytes.Buffer
44				if err := RunAggregate(newChunkReader(input, cuts...), 1000, &out, &late); err != nil {
45					t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
46				}
47			}
48			batch := time.Since(begin)
49			if avg := batch / time.Duration(iters); avg < best {
50				best = avg
51			}
52			if batch >= minBatch {
53				return best
54			}
55			// Run long enough to rise above scheduler noise, then try again.
56			iters *= 4
57		}
58		return best
59	}
60	
61	// TestAggregateLineCollectionCostFollowsBytesNotLineLength is the complexity
62	// guard. Two inputs have essentially the SAME total byte count and arrive
63	// through the SAME number of one-byte Reads; they differ only in whether the
64	// bytes form one very long physical record or thousands of short ones. A
65	// linear collector scans every byte about once either way (plus read-call
66	// overhead, identical per byte), so the two timings are comparable. The old
67	// collector rescanned the whole pending tail after every Read, i.e. about
68	// L*L/2 comparisons for one L-byte line versus only N*m/2 for N bytes split
69	// into m-byte lines, making the long-line input hundreds of times slower
70	// despite the identical byte and read counts.
71	func TestAggregateLineCollectionCostFollowsBytesNotLineLength(t *testing.T) {
72		if testing.Short() {

74		}

76	
77		// One long event record (long multibyte key) closed by a watermark.

82			``,

85		// The same number of bytes as many short newline-terminated records, all
86		// merging into one short-key window, closed by a watermark.
87		shortRecord := `{"type":"event","key":"短","time":100,"value":1}` + "\n"
88		var b strings.Builder

91		}

94

97		}
98		// The two streams must be genuinely the same order of size; otherwise the
99		// ratio would measure byte count rather than line layout.
100		if got := len(oneLongLine); got > target*2 || got < target {
101			t.Fatalf("test setup: long input %d bytes vs short input %d bytes", got, len(manyShortLines))
102		}
103	
104		// The timed long-line delivery must also stay correct: the whole key
105		// survives one-byte arrival and the watermark closes its window.
106		var out, late bytes.Buffer

108			t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
109		}
110		wantWindow := fmt.Sprintf(`{"key":%q,"start":0,"end":1000,"count":1,"sum":7}`+"\n", longKey)

164			t.Fatalf("one-shot reference failed: %v", err)
165		}
166	
167		// Alternating one-byte and 4 KiB cuts.
168		var cuts []int
169		pos := 0
170		small := true
171		for pos < len(input) {
172			step := 1
173			if !small {
174				step = 4096
175			}
176			small = !small
177			pos += step

12	// A partition number only identifies which independent input source a record
13	// came from; it must never enter the aggregate semantics: relabeling every
14	// partition number with a single bijection -- one that stays inside [0,N),
15	// neither merges two sources nor drops one, and is applied to EVERY record
16	// kind that carries a partition (events, watermarks and idle declarations) --
17	// must leave the window results byte-for-byte identical in content, row count
18	// and order, must leave every late notice identical in its event time, the
19	// watermark cited and the physical line number, and must keep a normal run
20	// successful. The only text allowed to change is the partition number named
21	// in an input error, which must be the relabeled number on the same physical
22	// line.
23	//
24	// The scenario is one business stream (window 1000, slide 600 -- 600 does not
25	// divide 1000) merged over THREE sources, one key "k", and the three sources
26	// play genuinely different roles that land on the zero, the maximum legal and
27	// a middle number:
28	//
29	//   - partition 0 (the zero index) is the source that races ahead;
30	//   - partition 2 (the maximum legal index for --partitions 3) is the source
31	//     that pins the overall effective watermark by lagging, then catches up;
32	//   - partition 1 (a middle index) is the source that goes idle and later
33	//     resumes with a legal watermark.
34	//
35	// The same key's events arrive from all three sources and, because the slide
36	// interval does not divide the window length, several of them land in more
37	// than one overlapping window. The stream first closes only the early window
38	// while the later overlapping window keeps receiving events. Source numbers
39	// never appear in the output. Everything goes through the public
40	// RunAggregatePartitionedSliding entry point; no production code, public entry
41	// point, result format or error convention is changed, and no renumbering
42	// command is introduced.

45	// bijection of {0,1,2} onto itself that moves every role off its original
46	// number: the fast source 0 -> 2 (now the maximum legal index), the idle
47	// source 1 -> 0 (now the zero index), the limiter 2 -> 1 (now a middle
48	// index), so each of zero/max/middle is exercised by a different source than
49	// before, while the total partition count stays 3.

53	// shown are the ORIGINAL labels; renumberPartitionFields applies the
54	// bijection. The blank-free layout keeps physical line numbers obvious.
55	//

57	//	line 2:  p1 event t=1000 v=3 -> [600,1600)

63	//	line 8:  p1 declares idle        (excluded from the minimum; effective stays 1000)

224		for _, start := range renumberWindowStarts {

231			}

251		for _, start := range []int64{600, 1200} {

375	// TestSlidingPartitionRenumberingPermutationIsABijection pins the labeling
376	// constraint itself: the relabeling must be a one-to-one correspondence onto
377	// {0,1,2}, stay in range and keep using the zero and the maximum legal index,
378	// so sources can never be merged or dropped.
379	func TestSlidingPartitionRenumberingPermutationIsABijection(t *testing.T) {
380		if !isPermutation(partitionRenumberPermutation, 3) {
381			t.Fatalf("the renumbering under test must be a bijection: %v", partitionRenumberPermutation)
382		}
383		// Maps that merge sources, drop a source, leave the range or keep a
384		// boundary role fixed must all be rejected by the same predicate.
385		for name, bad := range map[string]map[int64]int64{
386			"two sources merge into one": {0: 0, 1: 0, 2: 1},
387			"a source is dropped":        {0: 2, 1: 0},
388			"target out of range":        {0: 2, 1: 3, 2: 1},
389			"zero role never moves":      {0: 0, 1: 2, 2: 1},
390			"max role never moves":       {0: 1, 1: 0, 2: 2},
391		} {
392			if isPermutation(bad, 3) {
393				t.Errorf("%s must not be accepted as a renumbering bijection: %v", name, bad)
394			}
395		}
396	}

398	// isPermutation reports whether m is a bijection of {0,...,n-1} onto itself:
399	// every source is covered and maps to a distinct in-range target, the zero and
400	// maximum legal indices are both reused, and neither boundary role keeps its
401	// original number (so the safeguard genuinely moves the boundary roles).
402	func isPermutation(m map[int64]int64, n int64) bool {
403		if int64(len(m)) != n {
404			return false
405		}
406		seen := make(map[int64]bool)
407		for old, next := range m {
408			if old < 0 || old >= n || next < 0 || next >= n {
409				return false
410			}
411			if seen[next] {
412				return false
413			}
414			seen[next] = true
415		}
416		if !seen[0] || !seen[n-1] {
417			return false
418		}
419		if m[0] == 0 || m[n-1] == n-1 {
420			return false
421		}
422		return true
423	}

425	// assertPermutation fails the test unless m is a renumbering bijection.
426	func assertPermutation(t *testing.T, m map[int64]int64, n int64) {
427		t.Helper()
428		if !isPermutation(m, n) {
429			t.Fatalf("renumbering %v is not a bijection of [0,%d) onto itself", m, n)
430		}
431	}

433	// assertEveryPartitionFieldMapped compares two physical input streams that
434	// differ only in partition labels: every record keeps its type and line
435	// position, and each partition-bearing record (event, watermark and idle
436	// alike) carries exactly f(original). This proves no record kind was missed
437	// and no source was merged or relabeled inconsistently.
438	func assertEveryPartitionFieldMapped(t *testing.T, original, relabeled []string, f map[int64]int64) {
439		t.Helper()
440		if len(original) != len(relabeled) {
441			t.Fatalf("renumbering changed the record count: %d -> %d", len(original), len(relabeled))
442		}
443		kinds := map[string]int{}
444		for i, before := range original {
445			var o, rl map[string]json.RawMessage
446			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(before), &o); err != nil {
447				t.Fatalf("original line %d is not JSON: %v", i+1, err)
448			}
449			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(relabeled[i]), &rl); err != nil {
450				t.Fatalf("relabeled line %d is not JSON: %v", i+1, err)
451			}
452			if string(o["type"]) != string(rl["type"]) {
453				t.Errorf("line %d record type changed: %s -> %s", i+1, o["type"], rl["type"])
454			}
455			raw, ok := o["partition"]
456			if !ok {
457				t.Errorf("line %d (%s) carries no partition field to relabel", i+1, o["type"])
458				continue
459			}
460			var oldP int64
461			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &oldP); err != nil {
462				t.Fatalf("line %d partition is not an integer: %v", i+1, err)
463			}
464			var newP int64
465			if err := json.Unmarshal(rl["partition"], &newP); err != nil {
466				t.Fatalf("line %d relabeled partition is not an integer: %v", i+1, err)
467			}
468			if newP != f[oldP] {
469				t.Errorf("line %d (%s): partition %d relabeled to %d, want %d", i+1, o["type"], oldP, newP, f[oldP])
470			}
471			kinds[string(o["type"])]++
472		}
473		for _, kind := range []string{`"event"`, `"watermark"`, `"idle"`} {
474			if kinds[kind] == 0 {
475				t.Errorf("the stream must include %s records so that kind cannot be skipped by renumbering", kind)
476			}
477		}
478	}

480	// renumberPartitionFields returns the physical records with every record's
481	// partition field replaced by f(its old value). It rewrites events,
482	// watermarks and idle declarations with the single correspondence and leaves
483	// record order and all other fields untouched. Re-marshaling changes only
484	// formatting, never decoded content, so the engine sees an identical stream
485	// apart from source labels.
486	func renumberPartitionFields(t *testing.T, records []string, f map[int64]int64) []string {
487		t.Helper()
488		out := make([]string, len(records))
489		for i, line := range records {
490			var obj map[string]json.RawMessage
491			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
492				t.Fatalf("line %d is not JSON: %v", i+1, err)
493			}
494			raw, ok := obj["partition"]
495			if !ok {
496				t.Fatalf("line %d has no partition field to renumber: %s", i+1, line)
497			}
498			var p int64
499			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &p); err != nil {
500				t.Fatalf("line %d partition is not an integer: %v", i+1, err)
501			}
502			next, ok := f[p]
503			if !ok {
504				t.Fatalf("line %d: no renumbering target for source %d", i+1, p)
505			}
506			obj["partition"] = json.RawMessage(fmt.Sprintf("%d", next))
507			b, err := json.Marshal(obj)
508			if err != nil {
509				t.Fatalf("line %d could not be re-marshaled: %v", i+1, err)
510			}
511			out[i] = string(b)
512		}
513		return out
514	}

9	// Regression safeguards for the interaction between idle declarations and the
10	// effective (minimum) watermark when several active partitions tie on the
11	// minimum in partitioned sliding mode (window 1000, slide 600, three
12	// partitions, one key "k"):
13	//
14	//   - With the per-partition watermarks 1600/600/600 the effective watermark
15	//     is 600 and no window has closed. Declaring ONE of the two slow
16	//     partitions idle must not advance the effective watermark: the other,
17	//     still-active partition still pins it at 600, so no window may close
18	//     early. Only when that last holder of the minimum declares idle does the
19	//     remaining partition's 1600 become the effective watermark and close the
20	//     windows.
21	//   - While one minimum holder is idle, a legal event arriving from the other,
22	//     still-active minimum holder (time 1000, equal to the would-be window
23	//     edge and well above the effective 600) is judged against the effective
24	//     watermark 600 -- never against the fast partition's own 1600 -- so it is
25	//     neither reported late nor dropped; it joins the still-open overlapping
26	//     window.
27	//   - The window that closes last keeps the events both partitions
28	//     contributed before they went idle. The event at 1300 also belongs to
29	//     [1200,2200), which stays open at end of input and is never flushed.
30	//   - The rule is symmetric in which of the two tied partitions idles first,
31	//     and a repeated idle declaration for an already-idle partition is a
32	//     no-op: it neither advances the watermark nor re-emits any result while
33	//     the other slow partition stays active.
34	//
35	// Every check goes through the public RunAggregatePartitionedSliding entry
36	// point; output stays the existing line-per-JSON format with no partition
37	// field, and the normal path produces neither late notices nor errors.
38	
39	// tiedMinIdleBaseLines is the shared history physical lines 1-6:
40	//
41	//	line 1: p0 event time=700  value=2 -> [0,1000) and [600,1600)
42	//	line 2: p1 event time=1000 value=3 -> [600,1600)
43	//	line 3: p2 event time=1300 value=5 -> [600,1600) and [1200,2200)
44	//	line 4: p0 watermark 1600           -> fast partition races ahead
45	//	line 5: p1 watermark 600
46	//	line 6: p2 watermark 600            -> effective min = 600; nothing closes
47	//
48	// Windows in play start at 0, 600, 1200, ... with length 1000.
49	func tiedMinIdleBaseLines() []string {
50		return []string{
51			`{"type":"event","key":"k","time":700,"value":2,"partition":0}`,
52			`{"type":"event","key":"k","time":1000,"value":3,"partition":1}`,
53			`{"type":"event","key":"k","time":1300,"value":5,"partition":2}`,
54			`{"type":"watermark","time":1600,"partition":0}`,
55			`{"type":"watermark","time":600,"partition":1}`,
56			`{"type":"watermark","time":600,"partition":2}`,
57		}
58	}

60	// tiedMinIdleWantOutput is the exact, order-pinned output the full sequence
61	// must produce, with no partition field:
62	//
63	//   - [0,1000) holds only partition 0's time=700 event (the time=1000 events
64	//     sit on the right edge and must not leak back): count 1, sum 2.
65	//   - [600,1600) keeps both idle partitions' pre-idle contributions (2 from
66	//     p0, 3 from p1, 5 from p2) plus the still-active holder's legal event
67	//     after the first idle declaration (4): count 4, sum 14.
68	//
69	// [1200,2200) (holding the time=1300 event, count 1, sum 5) is not among the
70	// rows: it is still open when input ends.
71	var tiedMinIdleWantOutput = strings.Join([]string{
72		`{"key":"k","start":0,"end":1000,"count":1,"sum":2}`,
73		`{"key":"k","start":600,"end":1600,"count":4,"sum":14}`,
74		``,
75	}, "\n")

77	// TestSlidingPartitionTiedMinWatermarkNoClosureBeforeLastHolderIdles pins the
78	// output timing: after the three watermarks establish 600 as the effective
79	// minimum, neither that state nor the first idle declaration (nor repeated
80	// declarations of the same already-idle partition) may close any window,
81	// because the other slow partition is still active at 600. A legal event from
82	// that still-active partition after the first idle declaration is accepted
83	// with no late notice even though partition 0's own watermark is 1600.
84	func TestSlidingPartitionTiedMinWatermarkNoClosureBeforeLastHolderIdles(t *testing.T) {
85		cases := []struct {
86			name      string
87			firstIdle int64 // the slow partition that declares idle first (1 or 2)
88			active    int64 // the other slow partition, still active at 600
89		}{
90			{name: "partition 1 idles first, partition 2 holds the minimum", firstIdle: 1, active: 2},
91			{name: "partition 2 idles first, partition 1 holds the minimum", firstIdle: 2, active: 1},
92		}
93		for _, tc := range cases {
94			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
95				lines := tiedMinIdleBaseLines()
96				lines = append(lines,
97					`{"type":"idle","partition":`+pid(tc.firstIdle)+`}`,
98					// Repeating the already-idle declaration must stay a no-op.
99					`{"type":"idle","partition":`+pid(tc.firstIdle)+`}`,
100					`{"type":"idle","partition":`+pid(tc.firstIdle)+`}`,
101					// time 1000 >= effective 600: legal, joins [600,1600), closes
102					// nothing. It must not be judged late against p0's own 1600.
103					`{"type":"event","key":"k","time":1000,"value":4,"partition":`+pid(tc.active)+`}`,
104				)
105				stdout, stderr, err := runPartitionedSliding(t, strings.Join(lines, "\n"), 1000, 600, 3)
106				if err != nil {
107					t.Fatalf("unexpected error while the last minimum holder stays active: %v", err)
108				}
109				if stderr != "" {
110					t.Errorf("the active holder's time=1000 event must not be late vs effective 600, got notice %q", stderr)
111				}
112				if stdout != "" {
113					t.Errorf("no window may close while active partition %d still pins the effective watermark at 600, got output %q", tc.active, stdout)
114				}
115			})
116		}
117	}

119	// TestSlidingPartitionTiedMinWatermarkIdleSequence is the primary scenario:
120	// once the second (last active) holder of the minimum declares idle,
121	// partition 0's 1600 becomes the effective watermark and closes [0,1000) and
122	// [600,1600) in that order with the merged counts and sums, preserving the
123	// events both partitions contributed before idling. [1200,2200) stays open at
124	// end of input. The whole run produces no late notice and no error.
125	func TestSlidingPartitionTiedMinWatermarkIdleSequence(t *testing.T) {
126		lines := tiedMinIdleBaseLines()
127		lines = append(lines,
128			`{"type":"idle","partition":1}`,                                  // p1 leaves; p2 still active at 600
129			`{"type":"event","key":"k","time":1000,"value":4,"partition":2}`, // legal: joins [600,1600)
130			`{"type":"idle","partition":2}`,                                  // last minimum holder leaves: effective = 1600
131		)
132		stdout, stderr, err := runPartitionedSliding(t, strings.Join(lines, "\n"), 1000, 600, 3)
133		if err != nil {
134			t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
135		}
136		if stderr != "" {
137			t.Fatalf("normal processing must produce no late notice, got %q", stderr)
138		}
139		if stdout != tiedMinIdleWantOutput {
140			t.Fatalf("stdout mismatch:\n got: %q\nwant: %q", stdout, tiedMinIdleWantOutput)

142

163			fs.Usage()
164			return 2

166		windowSpecified := false
167		slideSpecified := false
168		partitionsSpecified := false
169		fs.Visit(func(f *flag.Flag) {

171			case "window-ms":

173			case "slide-ms":

完成。重构仅改动等待首次整体水位线的判定逻辑，入口行为全部保持。

## 问题根源

`effectiveWatermark()`（原 `edgefleet/aggregate.go:798`）在**每条**水位线/休眠记录到来时都从分区 0 扫描到 P-1。按编号升序上报、最后一个活跃分区迟迟不上报时，已确认的 P-1 个分区被反复检查，等待阶段为 O(分区数 × 记录数) 的平方级开销。

## 重构内容（`edgefleet/aggregate.go`）

用两个增量结构替代全量重扫：

- **`unreportedActive` 计数器**：初始为分区总数，每个分区只在第一次表态（首次水位线，或未上报即声明休眠）时减一；重复水位线、重复休眠、休眠后恢复都不会再次计数。等待是否结束变成 O(1) 判断，不触碰任何已确认分区。
- **按代际（generation）懒淘汰的最小堆 `watermarkHeap`**：每个活跃且已上报分区一个候选；休眠或恢复时仅推进该分区 generation，旧候选在升到堆顶时丢弃（每条记录摊销 O(log P)，整体随记录数近似线性）。水位线建立后的最小值推进规则与原来完全一致，只在全部休眠且从未产出时保持未知。

关键语义均保留并经测试覆盖：等待期间不提前判迟到/关窗；最后一个分区上报或被声明休眠的**当条记录**立即按剩余活跃分区最小值建水位线并关窗；全休眠从未建立时水位线未知、事件保留不输出；非法分区与倒退水位线不计入已满足条件，仍报物理行号并停止、已有结果保留。

## 验证

- 全部既有测试通过（`go test ./... -count=1`），含 `-race`、`-short`、`go vet`、gofmt；CLI 固定/滑动/分区/无分区四种模式冒烟一致。
- 新增 `aggregate_first_watermark_wait_test.go`：上报顺序（4 种排列）与休眠先后（3 种）输出不变性、等待期合法事件不被误判、重复记录不多计、全休眠事件保留、等待期非法行号，以及**复杂度计时守卫**——旧代码上升/下降顺序耗时比 **10.86（失败）**，新代码 **0.89（通过，阈值 6.0）**，并附 benchmark。
- 另做了 20,000 组随机流（含倒退、休眠/恢复越界、对休眠分区发事件）与 HEAD 旧实现的差分对比：窗口输出、迟到提示、错误类别与文本逐字节一致（验证用的临时代码包已删除）。
